BiblicalUsage: Raveh means sated, filled with drink. Moses warned of the man who blesses himself and says, 'I shall have peace, though I walk in the imagination of mine heart, to add drunkenness to thirst'; Isaiah promises, 'the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought'; and Jeremiah says the soul of God's people 'shall be as a watered garden.'
TheologicalSignificance: What this says to me is that satisfaction has two faces: the drunkard who adds drunkenness to thirst, and the soul that God satisfies in drought — and only one of them stays satisfied.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
